title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

providers.name: Atlassian Jira / Confluence Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Product IP allowlisting requires Premium/Enterprise. SAML SSO typically requires Atlassian Guard Standard or an included entitlement.

controls.name: User API tokens (authentication policy)
controls.what: Blocks members in a policy from creating new or using existing user API tokens against the org's apps; takes up to 10 minutes.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > Authentication policies > Edit > Block members from creating a new or using an existing API token
controls.quote: By default, your organization's user API token settings are set to allow access. With the user API token setting, you can allow or block members from: Creating a new API token Using an existing API token

controls.name: User API token expiration (authentication policy)
controls.what: Sets user API tokens of policy members to expire after 1-365 days (or never).
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > Authentication policies > Edit > Never expires / Expires
controls.quote: You can set the token to never expire or set a different expiration date in an authentication policy. You can set the token to expire between 1 to 365 days.

controls.name: API token access for external users
controls.what: Blocks external (unmanaged) users from calling app APIs with user API tokens, including existing tokens.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > External users > API token access for external users > Block
controls.quote: When you block user API token access for external users, they are unable to use a token to access app s through an app API, even if they previously used a token to access them.

controls.name: Revoke user API tokens
controls.what: Org admins can permanently revoke managed accounts' API tokens, singly or in bulk, or via the Delete API token API.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Insights > API token activity > Revoke
controls.quote: You can to revoke one or more of a managed account’s API tokens from one place.

controls.name: IP allowlists
controls.what: Users outside allowed IPs/locations cannot reach Jira/Confluence content, including via the APIs.
controls.setting: admin.atlassian.com > Security > Device security > IP allowlists
controls.plan: Premium (Jira, JSM, Confluence, Compass) or Enterprise (Analytics, Focus)
controls.quote: Users also won't be able to access that app programmatically via the APIs.

no_control.what: The Marketplace and custom app access control cannot block apps that use Atlassian API tokens.
no_control.quote: Marketplace, custom and other third-party app s that use Atlassian API tokens to access data

no_control.what: Admins cannot create or issue API tokens on a user's behalf (only users create them).
no_control.quote: It’s not possible for anyone else to create an API token on behalf of a user. Users must create API tokens themselves.

authentication.summary: Email + API token via Basic; scoped API tokens; delegated OAuth 2.0 (3LO) bearer tokens. Forge has a separate app model.

federation.details: General inbound external-IdP token exchange is not established for product REST APIs. SAML SSO alone does not replace API credentials.

ip_restriction.boundary: Site IP allowlists cover Jira/Confluence REST access. Organization administration and provisioning APIs have separate coverage and are excluded from site rules.

renewal.summary: The static API token is reused on each request until it expires (1 to 365 days); after that the user must create a new token. No refresh token is involved.

administration.summary: Token revocation, managed-account API-token controls, scopes, app access policies and app installation controls.
administration.conditions: Product IP allowlisting requires Premium/Enterprise. SAML SSO typically requires Atlassian Guard Standard or an included entitlement.

sso.details: Atlassian says API tokens and scripts keep working after SAML SSO is enforced; token use is governed by the separate User API tokens policy setting.

offboard.details: Deleting the account revokes token access, but deactivation or SCIM unsync does not remove site access and tokens stay usable until access is removed or tokens are revoked.

inventory.details: Atlassian Administration > Insights > API token activity (and the Get API tokens API) lists tokens created by managed accounts only.

reads.ui: Atlassian Administration > Insights > Audit log; filter activity "Viewed Jira issue" / "Viewed Confluence page" and the token owner

offboard.ui: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Users > Account type = Managed accounts > user > ••• > Delete account; or revoke tokens at Insights > API token activity > Revoke

token_format.notes: Atlassian Bamboo Javadoc says API tokens start with ATAT. Length is variable by design; no official regex. GitHub secret scanning has an atlassian_api_token partner pattern.

containment.steps: Admin: Insights > API token activity > Revoke (or DELETE /v1/orgs/{orgId}/api-tokens for all managed user tokens); owner: id.atlassian.com > Revoke / Revoke all. Optionally block user API token access via authentication policy; deactivate account.
containment.notes: Token is sent on each request (Basic/Bearer), so revocation stops further calls; propagation delay not documented for user tokens (service-account tokens: up to 10 min). Revocation is permanent.
